justification: Removing an edge removes a dependency/path and changes the causal theory.
Adding an edge introduces a new dependency/path and changes the causal theory.
Reversing an edge changes causal direction, ancestors, interventions and d-separation.
Renames an internal unmentioned variable while preserving graph structure over mentioned variables.
Edge subdivision is representation-like only if the verifier abstracts away direct-edge/path-length facts; current verifier may observe them.
Deleting a complete path intentionally removes causal support.
Chain replacement can be proof refactoring only if all external verifier consequences are preserved.
Merging nodes conflates variables/mechanisms and changes the theory.
Node split can be representation-preserving only if the split node is unmentioned and all verifier signatures are preserved.
Equal-interface subgraph replacement needs verifier audit; current signatures may expose internal structure.
Swapping branches changes which causes support which effects.
Alternative derivation changes direct-edge/path evidence under the current verifier.
